# Global Centroid-Moment-Tensor catalogue (one ndk release)

`gcmt` · adapter 1.0.0 · makes `moment_tensor` tokens

| | |
|---|---|
| Provider | The Global CMT Project (G. Ekström, M. Nettles), Lamont-Doherty |
| Home | https://www.globalcmt.org |
| Licence | `LicenseRef-GCMT-cite` |

## Terms

Free to download and use; the project asks that both reference papers be cited. No standard licence is stated, so Craton reads the file and never redistributes it.

## Cite

- Dziewonski, A. M., Chou, T.-A., Woodhouse, J. H. (1981). Determination of earthquake source parameters from waveform data for studies of global and regional seismicity. JGR 86, 2825-2852. doi:10.1029/JB086iB04p02825
- Ekström, G., Nettles, M., Dziewonski, A. M. (2012). The global CMT project 2004-2010: Centroid-moment tensors for 13,017 earthquakes. PEPI 200-201, 1-9. doi:10.1016/j.pepi.2012.04.002

## Access

One ndk file per release from the project's Lamont-Doherty server (the region names the URL and its sha256), downloaded once and cached by hash.

## From the source to the token

| Token slot | Comes from |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `event` |
| `lat, lon, depth_km` | the centroid (line 3), not the hypocentre |
| `time` | the hypocentre's time (line 1) plus the centroid time shift |
| `value` | Mrr, Mtt, Mpp, Mrt, Mrp, Mtp and M0 (lines 4-5), dyne·cm → N·m |
| `uncertainty` | each element's standard error (line 4); M0 its largest |
| `location_uncertainty` | the centroid's standard errors, where non-zero |
| `qualifiers` | event_id (the CMT name), source_type, depth_type |
| `resolution` | rupture length from Mw (Wells & Coppersmith 1994); 2× half duration |

## Uncertainty

Standard errors as GCMT reports them (formal, from the inversion: smaller than the true error). An element the inversion held fixed reports 0 and gets 1% of M0 instead.

## Known issues

- Complete from about Mw 5.5 worldwide (smaller where stations are dense); thin before 1977.
- Shallow quakes: Mrt and Mrp are poorly resolved and often fixed to zero.
- Centroid depths are below sea level, read here as below the ellipsoid (a few tens of metres apart at most, far below the depth error).
- Many World Stress Map records are single GCMT mechanisms: a task graded against WSM must leave its quake-based records out (CB-34 does).
